$comment: Config for scripts/art/build-atlases.js (npm run art:build). Paths are relative to art/vendor/.
Output: art/build/<sheet>.png (upload these), art/build/contact/<id>.png (check by eye),
src/shared/theme/packs/vale/layout.ts (generated, committed). See docs/ART.md task S3.
Facings in the output follow SpriteSetAsset (src/shared/theme/types.ts): facing d points at d * 360 / count
degrees counter-clockwise from screen right (zeroDeg 0, ccw true): 0 = right, 90 = up (away from the camera),
270 = down (towards the camera). Cells: start + d * (stride ?? frames) + f, row-major in the sheet.
noiseAlpha: source pixels with alpha <= noiseAlpha are cleared before anything else (Lords of Pain dithers its
soft shadows with alpha 1-2 noise over the whole 256 px frame, <= 0.8% opacity, invisible; without this the
crop box is the whole frame). pad: transparent pixels added around the union crop box on every side.
pivot: the feet, measured on `measure` (animation, facing, kept-frame index): body = pixels with alpha >
bodyAlpha and max(R, G, B) > bodyMinRgb (both packs bake a pure-black shadow, so 'lit' separates it from the
body; the alpha cut is per pack, see each set); pivot.y = the edge below the lowest body row; pivot.x = the
midpoint of the body pixels in the lowest footBand rows (between the outer edges of the feet), rounded. The
same frame's body height / bodyTiles gives pixelsPerTile (rounded to 0.1). Measured facing towards the camera
(the feet are side by side there, level with the root); the build prints the same measure for every facing.
outline (optional, enemies): { widthPx } writes <sheet>-outline.png beside each sheet, same size and cells: the
body mask above (so not the baked shadow) dilated per cell by a disc of radius widthPx (integer 1-4), white,
alpha = 255 - the sprite's alpha inside it. Drawn under the sprite and tinted, it is the contrast rim. Needs
pad >= widthPx + 1, so the rim is not clipped and keeps a transparent border for the bilinear filter.
SmallScaleInt knight, 'With shadows' sheets: 1920x1024 = 15 frames x 8 rows of 128x128.
Union box over the 8 animations is the whole 128x128 cell (Melee2 touches all four edges, Die the left,
right and bottom ones), so cells stay 128 with no pad: 8 x 8 = 64 cells fill a 1024x1024 atlas
exactly, so each animation gets its own atlas and keeps 8 of its 15 frames.
Kept frames: loops (idle, run) floor(i * 15 / 8) = 0,1,3,5,7,9,11,13 (even spacing round the cycle);
one-shots 0,2,...,14 (keeps the first and the final pose, which death holds).
rowOrderEvidence: Source row order is undocumented; determined by eye from Idle and Run crops (4x, mid-grey). The rows go
CLOCKWISE from screen right: row r faces (360 - 45 r) mod 360 degrees, so output facing d (ccw) = row (8 - d) % 8.
row 0 = right (0): Run leans and strides to the right, head leading on the right; Idle shield edge-on on the right.
row 1 = down-right (315): the shield's light outer face is visible, held to the right.
row 2 = down (270, towards camera): Idle shield face-on over the body's right half, sword hanging at
screen left, i.e. shield in the left hand and sword in the right as seen from the front; Run comes at the camera.
row 3 = down-left (225): shield outer face visible, held to the left.
row 4 = left (180): Run strides to the left, head leading on the left; Idle shield edge-on on the left.
row 5 = up-left (135): the shield's dark inner side is visible, top left.
row 6 = up (90, away from camera): shield inner side at screen left, sword upright at screen right (the back
view of the same left/right hands); Run seen from behind.
row 7 = up-right (45): shield inner side visible, top right.
Consistency check: the shield is held in front, so its outer face shows exactly on the rows with a
towards-camera component (1, 2, 3) and its inner side on the rows facing away (5, 6, 7). Reading the rows
counter-clockwise instead would put the outer face on rows 5-7, which it is not.
class.vanguard.pivotNote: The knight's baked shadow is black at alpha 200-239 (core ~216) and every body pixel has alpha >= 248, so alpha > 200 would count the shadow: the body cut is alpha > 240.

$comment: Lords of Pain skeleton: one 256x256 PNG per frame, <folder>/<facing>/<folder>_<facing>_<angle>_<frame>.png.
The folder angles are screen angles (E = 0, N = 90, counter-clockwise), the output convention already;
the script rebuilds each file name from d * 22.5 and fails if it does not exist, so the order below is checked.
By eye: E/W stride right/left, N shows the back (spine and pelvis, skull clear above the shoulders),
S the front (ribcage, skull bowed over the chest towards the camera).
Union box (alpha > noiseAlpha) is 92x68 + 3 px pad = 98x74: 10 per row, 13 rows, so walk and death get
one 980x962 atlas each (one 1024 atlas holds 130 cells; the two need 256). Stand-ins (docs/ART.md S5): idle
and hit = walk frame 0 held (frames 1, stride 8), attack = the walk's cells.
enemy.swarmer.pivotNote: The skeleton's shadow is black at alpha <= ~140; its thin bones are anti-aliased (only ~20 pixels per frame reach 255), so alpha > 200 would drop the shins: the body cut is lit pixels at alpha > 64.
enemy.swarmer.outlineNote: Enemy contrast rim (enemy outline plan O3, decision E4: 2 art px, tunable 1-3 in Studio). pad 3 = widthPx + 1; it was 1, so the cells grew from 94x70 and the pivot moved by (2, 2) with them.

tile.biome.1.floor.$comment: 256x256, opaque, seamless: used whole. meanHex = rounded mean sRGB of all pixels (the biome.1 floor colour).
tile.biome.1.floor.name: tile-biome1-floor

ui.ring.player.$comment: Soft ring; cropped to alpha > noiseAlpha + pad. Pivot = centre of the crop (the ring sits centred under the player).
ui.ring.player.name: ui-ring-player

ui.marker.pedestal.$comment: 2 px vertical beam; cropped to alpha > noiseAlpha + pad. Pivot = bottom centre (the beam rises from the pedestal).
ui.marker.pedestal.name: ui-marker-pedestal

$comment: World art (docs/DECOR.md R5), the Lords of Pain props, effects and breakables: scripts/art/build-atlases.js
'World art' explains every field. Output: <atlas.name>.png (+ -2, ... if it overflows), the `own` files, contact
sheets art/build/contact/decor.<piece>.png and VALE_WORLD_LAYOUTS in layout.ts. Drawn at the skeleton's scale
(pixelsPerTileFrom): the pack renders every prop at the same scale as its characters.
noiseAlpha: the pack's dithered shadow noise (alpha 1-2), cleared. shadowRgb: the baked shadow is pure black (max
RGB <= 4 over thousands of pixels; bodies have almost none: column1 has 0 opaque body pixels at <= 4), so
`shadow: false` clears max(R, G, B) <= 4. flames: clearRgbBelow 80 drops the grey smoke column (max RGB <= 72)
above the fire (>= ~95), which would otherwise make the cell 158 px tall. pad: transparent pixels round every
cell / rect (bilinear filtering never reaches a neighbour). footBand: rows for the bottom / top pivot midpoints.
mote: the ambient particle texture of every biome, zone.png (a soft white disc) at 1/16, alpha stretched to 255
(the emitter's Transparency sets the look), RGB white (the emitter's Color tints it); its own file, since a
ParticleEmitter.Texture takes no ImageRect. zone: the stairwell disc at 1/4 (676 px of soft disc is far more
than the 2.6 tiles it is drawn at).
Names are art names; packs/vale/manifest.ts maps decor / breakable IDs onto them (the same art for all five biomes).
Standing pieces (tall / low on far-wall tops, the wall torch, breakables) drop the baked shadow (`shadow: false`):
their billboards are held to a small box (DECOR_BOX, BREAKABLE_VIEW.maxHeightTiles) and a shadow there only shrinks
the body. Flat pieces keep it (it lies on the floor, where they are drawn).
Facings (docs/DECOR.md 'Facings'): the camera's world axes land at 39.3 / 140.7 degrees on screen and the wall
normals the plan uses, (1, 0) and (0, 1), at 320.7 / 219.3, so grid pieces use the pack's diagonal renders (NE,
NW, SW, SE: edges at ~34 degrees). `facings: { count: 4, zeroDeg: 45 }` puts the output facings on exactly those
(facing 2 = 225, 3 = 315: the normals land 39 degrees inside their bins). DecorController picks a grid piece's
facing from its wall normal (decorFacingDir), so: the torch points along the normal (artOffsetDeg 0: normal SW ->
the SW render, the cup sticking out of the wall towards the room); a wall segment RUNS perpendicular to it (the
pack's wall renders run along their own facing, so artOffsetDeg 90: normal SW (run along the other axis, 140.7) ->
the SE render). Square / round single pieces (columns, brazier, barrel, crate) need one facing: NE (grid-aligned).
Round flat pieces take a few facings as variants (.1..), picked by cell hash.
Picked by eye from per-facing montages: wall2/wall3 E renders run horizontally, N vertically, NE at ~34 degrees;
the torch's E render leans its cup to the right of its bracket (it sticks out along its facing).
Sprite effects (docs/FX_AUDIO.md F2): one-facing flipbooks for the theme's fx.* IDs, all packed into ONE atlas
(art/build/<atlas>.png, <= 1024 a side) and described by the generated src/shared/theme/packs/vale/fxLayout.ts.
Source: horizontal strips of `frames` cells `frameW` wide (the strip's full height); the build fails unless the
strip is exactly frames x frameW wide. `keep` (optional): the strip frames used, in play order (default all).
`preview`: what the strip's Preview.gif shows, measured with PIL (frame count, ms per frame); fps = 1000 / ms
unless `fps` overrides it. `previewNote` records every mismatch between the GIF and the strip. `grey`:
desaturate to luminance (integer Rec. 601 weights) and stretch so the set's brightest pixel is white, alpha kept,
so ImageColor3 can tint it to a theme role; an untinted set (grey false) gets its alpha-weighted mean colour
(meanColor) for the enemy-bullet colour rule. `burst` (optional): the strip's frames are separate pieces (a
particle strip), composed into a `frames`-frame burst in a `cell` x `cell` square: piece k flies from the centre
along dirs[k % dirs.length] (per-mille unit vectors, integer maths), radiusFrom -> radiusTo px, fading out
linearly from frame fadeFrom. Each set is cropped to its union alpha box (+ pad); its pivot is the box centre.
Packing: each set is one band of rows at a y that is a multiple of its frame height (so SpriteSetAsset's
`start + f` cell formula addresses it in the shared atlas), bands sorted by frame height; the atlas width is
the one with the smallest area.

$comment: Ambient particle textures (docs/FX_AUDIO.md F6) for the decor.fx.ambient.b<n> ParticleEmitters, one PNG each
(art/build/<name>.png): `grid` x `grid` square cells of a power-of-two side (the strip frame centred in each), so
a ParticleEmitter flipbook (FlipbookLayout Grid2x2 / Grid4x4 / Grid8x8) can play them; grid 1 is a single
frame (no flipbook). `cells`: the strip frame shown in each cell, row-major (default: evenly resampled from
the strip). Always grey (luminance stretched to white): the emitter's Color is the biome's ambient role. `fps`
and `mode` (Loop, OneShot = once over a particle's life, PingPong, Random) go into the theme's particle
flipbook. Grim (b4) has no match in the pack and keeps no texture.
